title: cross-team-engineering-leadership-weekly-staff-notes-2026-04-27
content:
Cross-team engineering leadership weekly staff notes - 2026-04-27

Attendees: Jordan Lee (chair), Priya Nair, Evan Chen, Sara Gomez, Liam O'Connor, Mei Wang, Alex Park (observability), Nora Patel (release-eng), Carlos Ruiz (platform), several team leads dialed in.

Objective: Weekly alignment across serving-runtime, infra/platform, observability, release-engineering, and product for near-term rollouts, SLOs, and high-priority bugs.

1) Quick wins / kudos
- Serving-runtime: +20% throughput improvement on medium-batch path after kernel selection tweak (shipped in canary yesterday). Great cross-team debugging between infra and runtime.
- Observability: New per-model cost breakdown landed in Console beta; early feedback from two customers looks promising.

2) Production incidents / health
- Incident summary (past 7 days): two transient elevated p99 tail spikes during a multi-region deployment test. Root cause: KV-cache invalidation race in the cold-start path when autoscaler added nodes (related to ENG-4521). No customer-facing outages; SRE escalated during test.
- Metrics: p50 latency stable; p95 improved slightly; p99 increased from 780ms -> 1.1s during the spike window. Token cost delta negligible.

3) Serving-runtime updates
- Canary rollout: rta-model-v2.1 (int8 quantized) is in 10% canary for hosted API. Early perf: 30% token-cost reduction vs v2.0 and 1.2x latency on long context (expected). Need to validate quality on the eval suite (Priya).
- KV cache bug: identified race when node join + concurrent prefix-insert triggers double-free of cache pointer. Fix proposed and patch in review (PR #1287). Plan: hotfix to canary fleet tonight; full rollout after 48h observation.
- Memory leakage: small leak observed in long-running chat sessions on 80-token window; suspected in attention cache cleanup. Investigation ongoing (Evan + Mei).

4) Platform / Dedicated capacity
- Dedicated: planning for next quarter capacity uplift for two enterprise customers (estimate: +40% GPU days). Need final Q2 pricing approval from Product Finance by 2026-05-04. (Carlos to follow up).
- Autoscaling policy: added a cooldown to reduce churn observed during load spikes; will monitor.

5) Observability & SLOs
- New trace sampling knobs deployed; sample rate default lowered to reduce ingestion cost but retained high-sampling for error traces.
- SLO review: suggestion to adjust p99 objective for large-context routes from 1.2s -> 1.0s but team flagged risk with current canary latency on quantized model. Decision deferred until canary quality evals complete.

6) Release engineering / rollouts
- Canary cadence: move to weekly canary snapshots (previously bi-weekly) for faster iteration. Nora to update canary playbook and notify CS/PD.
- Rollback drill scheduled 2026-05-02 across regions; will simulate regional capacity failure and verify fallback to compatible model variants.

7) Developer experience / SDKs
- Streaming API: adding better partial-error semantics to make retries easier for clients; draft PR open. SDK teams want to add an opt-in client-side dedupe for identical streaming requests (to reduce duplicate tokens during flakey networks).

8) Product / customer asks
- Two enterprise customers requested guaranteed throughput windows for batch embedding jobs; product wants a dedicated queue proposal. Platform/Serving to propose architecture options by 2026-05-07.

9) Open blockers / risks
- Quality risk: int8 quantized canary shows occasional hallucination regressions on retrieval-augmented prompts. Priya to run targeted eval sets to quantify.
- Operational risk: KV-cache race could impact autoscaling in edge cases; hotfix timeline is critical.
- Cost risk: lowering trace sampling reduces observability fidelity; Ops wants manual toggles per-customer for high-value accounts.

10) Decisions made
- Proceed with extended canary (10% -> 30%) only after: (a) PR patch for KV cache is deployed to canary and observed for 48h, (b) targeted evals show <1% regression in QA metrics.
- Rollback drill on 2026-05-02 approved.

11) Action items (owner - description - Jira/PR - due)
- Evan Chen - Push KV-cache hotfix to canary fleet and monitor for 48h - JIRA ENG-4521 / PR #1287 - due 2026-04-28
- Priya Nair - Run targeted quality evals for rta-model-v2.1 (int8) on retrieval prompt set; share report - JIRA ENG-4589 - due 2026-04-30
- Carlos Ruiz - Finalize Dedicated capacity uplift pricing proposal and sync with Product Finance - JIRA DED-211 - due 2026-05-04
- Nora Patel - Update canary playbook with weekly cadence + rollback runbook; coordinate drill - Confluence: ENG-Canary-Playbook - due 2026-04-29
- Alex Park - Add temporary high-sampling toggle for specified enterprise customers in Console (ops-only control) - JIRA INFRA-337 - due 2026-05-05
- Mei Wang - Investigate memory leak in long-running chat sessions and post interim mitigation (heap profiling + guardrails) - JIRA ENG-4620 - due 2026-05-03

12) Notes to follow up / parking lot
- Evaluate automated model-quality gating (policy) for canary promotion.
- Consider short-term contraction of trace retention for non-critical models to control cost.
- Revisit SLO targets after canary completes.

Next meeting: 2026-05-04 (same time).

Minutes prepared by Jordan Lee. Raw chat log and related artifacts saved to linked_artifacts.

Informal notes / scratch:
- Need a quick comms blurb for Sales & CS once canary moves to 30% (short template: what changed, expected perf and quality windows, rollback plan). Priya offered to draft.
- Small todo: confirm CFO approval timeline for dedicated pricing (Carlos to ping).

(End of notes)
